judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports are highly thorough and hit all four expectations with nearly equivalent substance and specificity; Report 2 is slightly more structured (explicit wave/table layout) but the two are comparable in coverage and correctness.

report_1.evidence: Engineer C — registry config: F-02, F-05, F-09, owning pipeline/registry.py. Three one-line edits to an 11-line file should be one small PR, not three conflicting ones.

report_2.evidence: pipeline/registry.py (12 lines) is hit by F-02 ..., F-05 ..., and F-09 ... — splitting three one-liners across engineers buys no speed and guarantees conflicts, so they bundle.

report_1.evidence: Ordering across streams: after triage, all streams start simultaneously — there are no cross-stream file dependencies. ... Engineer A — batch runner: F-04+F-13 (merged), F-07, F-14, plus test F-12 ... Engineer B — scoring and rubric: F-01 plus its test F-11 ... Engineer C — registry config: F-02, F-05, F-09

report_2.evidence: Wave 1 runs batches A–D fully in parallel — they are file-disjoint by construction, so four engineers can work simultaneously with zero merge contact. Wave 2 is batch E plus the F-03 half of D, both gated on external answers

report_1.evidence: F-06 — a policy decision disguised as a fix. "Tighten the thresholds so borderline answers score lower" names no target values, and no correct values are derivable from the repo ... Assign it only once concrete values and sign-off exist.

report_2.evidence: F-06 — escalate, don't assign. ... that's a scoring-policy decision, not a bug with a determinable fix. It needs the reviewer/owner to supply concrete values, ideally with a before/after re-score of a known dataset, before anyone writes code.

report_1.evidence: tests/conftest.py:4 defaults RESULTS_DB to the machine-global path /var/tmp/llm-scoring/results.db; engineers running suites concurrently on a shared box could collide unless each overrides the env var. ... Export RESULTS_DB to a per-engineer path to avoid the shared /var/tmp/llm-scoring/results.db default in tests/conftest.py:4.

report_2.evidence: tests/conftest.py:4 defaults the suite's results database to a machine-global path: RESULTS_DB = os.environ.get("RESULTS_DB", "/var/tmp/llm-scoring/results.db"). Engineers ... running tests concurrently without overriding RESULTS_DB collide on that file and get flaky cross-contaminated runs.
